source.title: Enhanced conditioning produced by surprising increases in reinforcer value are unaffected by lesions of the amygdala central nucleus

confidence_rationale: Disconfirming-direction evidence for the CeA grounding of MECH-598's trigger. When surprise is produced by an unexpected ADDED event, enhanced conditioning is intact after CeA lesions; the CeA route is preferentially engaged by OMISSIONS. MECH-598's trigger is an unexpected aversive delivery, which is the presentation case. Mixed rather than weakens because the enhancement measured here may be Rescorla-Wagner US-effectiveness rather than Pearce-Hall associability, so it bounds the CeA citation without refuting the mechanism.
failure_signatures: Surprise produced by an unexpected ADDITIONAL outcome enhanced learning equally in CeA-lesioned and sham rats, so CeA-dependent associability is not the route for presentation-type surprise.

Citing CeA-dependent surprise-induced associability (Holland & Schiffino 2016) as the substrate for an aversive-DELIVERY trigger is contradicted by this lab's own omission-vs-presentation dissociation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: CeA lesions interfere with surprise-induced enhancement of event processing when surprise is produced by omitting an expected event, but not when it is produced by presenting an unexpected additional event (sucrose after food); CeA circuitry is preferentially engaged by omissions.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-598 names a phasic aversive PE (an unexpected negative change in valued self-state) as the trigger, which in the harm case is usually an unexpected DELIVERY of damage. This paper says the best-characterised CeA associability route does not handle presentation-type surprise, at least appetitively. So the CeA citation in the claim notes cannot stand as the substrate for the trigger without qualification.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Appetitive; the unexpected event is a reward increment, not harm. Unblocking-by-added-outcome is plausibly a Rescorla-Wagner effect, so this is a boundary on the CeA mapping rather than evidence against aversive associability. The human aversive studies (Li 2011, Zhang 2016) are the relevant counterweight.
mapping.source_context: Rat, light-noise compound unblocking with unexpected sucrose, excitotoxic CeA lesions

confidence_components.notes: Single experiment, modest N typical of the lab. Its value is as a boundary on a specific citation, not as a test of MECH-598 as a whole.
